589: The strength of the B family is that neither interpolation functions nor an assumption about short-range order is needed, and short-range order and defect interactions enter automatically. Its weaknesses are that each boundary point needs an MC/MD run (a sweep over Δμ × T), that solid–liquid transitions rarely occur during a simulation so TI or an interface method is needed separately, and that the width of ordered phases must be obtained by sublattice analysis in post-processing. This workflow belongs to the A family (table of stage 05 + analytic entropy terms → convex hull of stage 06); rk is merely the choice for joining the 11 liquid compositions smoothly. If it were replaced, a σ-weighted smoothing spline would be the smallest change. The B family is tried through route B (direct SGC MC, Ag–Cu) and its boundaries are compared with the A family (ideal mixing + RK fcc gap). The difference between the two is an estimate of the error due to short-range order and the interpolation functions.
